event_checks.event: Abel keeps sheep and Cain tills the ground
event_checks.reason: Genesis 4:2 states Abel was a keeper of sheep and Cain a tiller of the ground.

event_checks.event: Both bring offerings to the LORD
event_checks.reason: Genesis 4:3-4 records Cain bringing fruit of the ground and Abel bringing firstlings of his flock.

event_checks.event: God warns Cain that sin lieth at the door
event_checks.reason: Genesis 4:7 contains the words 'sin lieth at the door'. The speaker (the LORD, 4:6) is not in the quoted verse but is clear from context.

event_checks.event: Cain rises up against Abel in the field
event_checks.reason: Genesis 4:8 says that in the field Cain rose up against Abel and slew him.

event_checks.event: God sets a mark upon Cain
event_checks.reason: Genesis 4:15 says the LORD set a mark upon Cain.

event_checks.event: Hannah prays in bitterness of soul at Shiloh
event_checks.reason: 1:10 says she was in bitterness of soul and prayed. Shiloh is not named in 1:10 itself, but 1:9 places the scene at Shiloh, so this is minor context.

event_checks.event: Eli thinks she is drunken
event_checks.reason: 1:13 states that Eli thought she had been drunken.

event_checks.event: Hannah bears a son and names him Samuel
event_checks.reason: 1:20 states that she bare a son and called his name Samuel.

event_checks.event: She lends the child to the LORD
event_checks.reason: 1:28: 'I have lent him to the LORD.'

event_checks.event: Hannah prays: My heart rejoiceth in the LORD
event_checks.reason: 2:1 quotes this opening of her prayer directly.

event_checks.event: Rahab hides the two spies
event_checks.reason: Joshua 2:4 states the woman took the two men and hid them.

event_checks.event: Israel crosses the Jordan on dry ground
event_checks.reason: Joshua 3:17 states all the Israelites passed over on dry ground.

event_checks.event: The people march around the city once a day for six days
event_checks.reason: Joshua 6:14 says 'they compassed the city once... so they did six days.' The first day is in 6:11, so citing 6:11-14 would be slightly fuller, but the summary is accurate.

event_checks.event: On the seventh day they compass the city seven times
event_checks.reason: Joshua 6:15 states this explicitly.

event_checks.event: The wall falls down flat
event_checks.reason: Joshua 6:20 states the wall fell down flat after the shout.

event_checks.event: God tells Abraham to take Isaac to the land of Moriah
event_checks.reason: Genesis 22:2 explicitly commands Abraham to take Isaac and go into the land of Moriah.

event_checks.event: Abraham rises early and saddles his ass
event_checks.reason: Genesis 22:3 states Abraham rose up early in the morning and saddled his ass.

event_checks.event: Isaac asks where the lamb is
event_checks.reason: Genesis 22:7 records Isaac asking, 'where is the lamb for a burnt offering?'

event_checks.event: The angel of the LORD calls out of heaven
event_checks.reason: Genesis 22:11 states the angel of the LORD called unto him out of heaven.

event_checks.event: A ram caught in a thicket is offered instead
event_checks.reason: Genesis 22:13 describes the ram caught in a thicket by his horns, offered in the stead of his son.

event_checks.event: Pharaoh orders every son born to be cast into the river
event_checks.reason: Exodus 1:22 states this directly.

event_checks.event: Baby Moses is hidden in an ark of bulrushes
event_checks.reason: Exodus 2:3 describes the ark of bulrushes. Strictly, she placed him in it after she could no longer hide him, but the paraphrase is acceptable. The child is not yet named Moses, which is a minor point.

event_checks.event: Pharaoh's daughter finds the child
event_checks.reason: Exodus 2:5-6 states this directly.

event_checks.event: Moses flees to the land of Midian
event_checks.reason: Exodus 2:15 states this directly.

event_checks.event: God speaks from the burning bush
event_checks.reason: Exodus 3:2-4 describes God calling to Moses out of the midst of the bush.

event_checks.event: All the earth has one language
event_checks.reason: Genesis 11:1 states the whole earth was of one language and one speech.

event_checks.event: People settle in a plain in the land of Shinar
event_checks.reason: Genesis 11:2 says they found a plain in the land of Shinar and dwelt there.

event_checks.event: They make brick and plan a city and a tower
event_checks.reason: Genesis 11:3-4 describes making and burning brick, then the plan to build a city and a tower.

event_checks.event: The LORD comes down to see the city
event_checks.reason: Genesis 11:5 says the LORD came down to see the city and the tower.

event_checks.event: Their language is confounded and they are scattered
event_checks.reason: Verse 7 gives the LORD's resolve to confound their language, and verse 8 records the scattering. Verse 9 states the confounding outright, but the paraphrase is a fair summary of 7-8.

event_checks.event: Israel camps before the mount
event_checks.reason: Exodus 19:2 states 'there Israel camped before the mount.'

event_checks.event: Mount Sinai smokes as the LORD descends
event_checks.reason: Exodus 19:18 says the mount was 'altogether on a smoke, because the LORD descended upon it in fire.'

event_checks.event: God speaks the ten commandments
event_checks.reason: Exodus 20:1-3 records God speaking 'all these words' and gives the opening commandment. The full list continues through 20:17, but the cited verses support the event.

event_checks.event: The people make a golden calf
event_checks.reason: In Exodus 32:4 Aaron fashions the calf from the gold the people gave him (32:1-3). Attributing the making to 'the people' is a fair summary, since 32:35 says 'they made the calf, which Aaron made.'

event_checks.event: Moses hews two new tables of stone
event_checks.reason: Exodus 34:1 is the LORD's command to hew the tables. Moses actually does so in 34:4 ('And he hewed two tables of stone like unto the first'). The event is still clearly supported in context.

event_checks.event: The sisters send word that Lazarus is sick
event_checks.reason: John 11:3 states the sisters sent word that the one Jesus loved was sick.

event_checks.event: Jesus arrives after Lazarus has lain in the grave four days
event_checks.reason: John 11:17 says Jesus found that Lazarus had lain in the grave four days already.

event_checks.event: Jesus says: I am the resurrection, and the life
event_checks.reason: John 11:25 quotes this exactly. Jesus says it to Martha.

event_checks.event: Jesus weeps
event_checks.reason: John 11:35 reads 'Jesus wept.'

event_checks.event: Lazarus comes forth bound with graveclothes
event_checks.reason: John 11:44 describes Lazarus coming forth bound hand and foot with graveclothes.

event_checks.event: A little maid tells of the prophet in Samaria
event_checks.reason: Verse 3 records her words to her mistress about the prophet in Samaria. The cited verse says only 'she', but verse 2 identifies her as the little maid.

event_checks.event: The king of Israel rends his clothes
event_checks.reason: Verse 7 states that he rent his clothes after reading the letter.

event_checks.event: Elisha says to wash in Jordan seven times
event_checks.reason: Verse 10 records Elisha sending a messenger with the instruction to wash in Jordan seven times. The event wording omits the messenger, which is acceptable paraphrase.

event_checks.event: Naaman turns away in a rage
event_checks.reason: Verse 12 says 'he turned and went away in a rage'.

event_checks.event: His flesh comes again like a little child's
event_checks.reason: Verse 14 says his flesh came again like unto the flesh of a little child.

event_checks.event: Nebuchadnezzar sets up an image of gold
event_checks.reason: Daniel 3:1 explicitly states the king made an image of gold and set it up in the plain of Dura.

event_checks.event: Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego refuse to worship it
event_checks.reason: Daniel 3:12 is the Chaldeans' accusation that the three 'serve not thy gods, nor worship the golden image'. This adequately supports their refusal, which they confirm in 3:16-18.

event_checks.event: The furnace is heated seven times hotter
event_checks.reason: Daniel 3:19 records the command to heat the furnace 'one seven times more than it was wont to be heated'.

event_checks.event: The king sees four men loose in the fire
event_checks.reason: Daniel 3:25 states 'I see four men loose, walking in the midst of the fire'.

event_checks.event: They come out with no smell of fire upon them
event_checks.reason: Daniel 3:27 says 'nor the smell of fire had passed on them'. Their coming out is in 3:26, and 3:27 presupposes it. This is acceptable paraphrase.

event_checks.event: Nehemiah weeps over the news of Jerusalem
event_checks.reason: Nehemiah 1:4 says he sat down and wept upon hearing the words about Jerusalem.

event_checks.event: King Artaxerxes asks why his countenance is sad
event_checks.reason: Nehemiah 2:1-2 records the king asking, 'Why is thy countenance sad?'

event_checks.event: Nehemiah views the walls by night
event_checks.reason: Nehemiah 2:13 says he went out by night and viewed the walls.

event_checks.event: Sanballat and Tobiah mock the builders
event_checks.reason: Nehemiah 4:1-3 records Sanballat mocking the Jews and Tobiah adding his fox taunt. Earlier mockery in 2:19 also comes after the night inspection, so the order still holds.

event_checks.event: The wall is finished in fifty and two days
event_checks.reason: Nehemiah 6:15 states the wall was finished in fifty and two days.

event_checks.event: Zacchaeus, a chief among the publicans, seeks to see Jesus
event_checks.reason: Luke 19:2-3 calls him the chief among the publicans and says he sought to see Jesus. 'A chief' versus 'the chief' is minor paraphrase.

event_checks.event: He climbs up into a sycomore tree
event_checks.reason: Luke 19:4 says he climbed up into a sycomore tree to see him.

event_checks.event: Jesus says: to day I must abide at thy house
event_checks.reason: Luke 19:5 quotes this saying directly.

event_checks.event: The people murmur
event_checks.reason: Luke 19:7 says they all murmured.

event_checks.event: Zacchaeus gives half his goods to the poor
event_checks.reason: In Luke 19:8 Zacchaeus declares 'the half of my goods I give to the poor'. This is a spoken statement or pledge, not a narrated act of giving. It is close enough as paraphrase, though 'declares he gives' would be more precise.

event_checks.event: A great multitude follows Jesus
event_checks.reason: John 6:2 states a great multitude followed him.

event_checks.event: Jesus asks Philip where to buy bread
event_checks.reason: John 6:5 records Jesus asking Philip, 'Whence shall we buy bread?'

event_checks.event: Andrew tells Jesus of a lad with five barley loaves and two small fishes
event_checks.reason: John 6:8-9 matches this nearly verbatim.

event_checks.event: The men sit down and Jesus gives thanks
event_checks.reason: John 6:10-11: the men sat down and Jesus gave thanks.

event_checks.event: Twelve baskets of fragments are gathered
event_checks.reason: John 6:13: twelve baskets were filled with fragments.

event_checks.event: Saul consents to Stephen's death
event_checks.reason: Acts 8:1 states 'Saul was consenting unto his death.' The death referred to is Stephen's, per the end of Acts 7.

event_checks.event: A light from heaven shines around Saul near Damascus
event_checks.reason: Acts 9:3 says this directly.

event_checks.event: Saul is three days without sight
event_checks.reason: Acts 9:9 says this directly.

event_checks.event: Ananias lays his hands on Saul
event_checks.reason: Acts 9:17: 'putting his hands on him.'

event_checks.event: Saul preaches Christ in the synagogues
event_checks.reason: Acts 9:20 says this directly.
